questions: Which controller change (kp, kd, ki, weight shape or line_loss mode) produced the iteration 8 gain, and how did s-bend and slalom line_loss_events move per run? Report counts and off-track counts per track.
Did the oval hold at 16/20 or better with steering_oscillation under about 0.35? The oval reached 20/20 with oscillation 0.22, so a drop would point to the controller change.

For slalom at 0/20 with line-loss 1.9, do the line losses cluster at direction changes between opposite bends? If so, does the line_loss mode (last_direction versus search) matter more than the sensor layout?
Is s-bend line-loss 1.05 a real plateau, or does a further controller step (for example kd) reduce it below 1.0 without raising oval oscillation?
feedback_request.suggested_changes_to_test: Keep the geometry fixed. If slalom line-loss stays near 1.9 with the controller change, test line_loss mode and kd on the controller side, not sensor geometry. Do not change wheel_track, span, footprint, sensor y or mass in the next iteration unless the controller change clearly fails on all tracks.

intent: Hold the iteration 8 geometry unchanged (best score 610.7): five sensors at x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 m with y = 0.07 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, wheel_track 0.09 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.16 m, mass 0.5 kg. The Integrator should keep changing only the controller response on the sharp tracks. Success is s-bend finishes holding at 15/20 or better and slalom line-loss falling below 1.9 per run, with the oval staying at 16/20 or better. Any score change should be attributable to the controller alone.
learning: Iteration 8 shows that with mass 0.5 kg and wheel_track 0.09 m, the controller response was the main remaining lever on s-bend (2/20 to 15/20 finishes). Geometry is now at its tested best, so the next gain is most likely from controller tuning. Slalom line-loss at 1.9 is unchanged by every geometry test, so its cause is probably the controller's response at direction changes or the line-loss mode.
rationale: Iteration 8 scored 610.7, the best so far, up from 400.0 in iteration 7. The geometry was held at the iteration 7 values and only the controller changed, so the gain came from controller response, not body geometry. Oval finished 20/20 (max_error 0.0195 m, oscillation 0.22). s-bend finished 15/20, up from 2/20, with line-loss 1.05, max_error 0.037 m and mean progress 0.96. Slalom is still 0/20 with line-loss 1.9 and max_error 0.065 m, so it is the remaining gap. My decision rule (a) for holding geometry was that s-bend line-loss is at or below 1.0 and the oval holds at 16/20 or better. The oval condition is met by a wide margin, and s-bend line-loss at 1.05 is within 0.05 of the threshold, with finishes now at 75%. The geometry evidence points to the same conclusion: span (iteration 2), footprint (iteration 3), forward position (iteration 4), wheel_track (iterations 5 and 6, now at its 0.09 m floor) and mass (iteration 7) have each been tested. The one geometry change that clearly helped was the mass drop to 0.5 kg, and that is now confirmed with a stronger controller. I therefore propose no geometry change. Changing geometry now would confound the controller result, and with only two iterations left the safest gain is a stable platform. I hold every value at the iteration 8 best. Slalom at 0/20 with line-loss 1.9 and max_error near 0.065 m is probably a line-loss mode or sharp direction-change problem, not a sensing gap, since footprint and span changes did not reduce its line-loss. The next question for the Integrator is whether the slalom losses occur at direction changes. Because the final race uses an unseen track of a different shape, I keep the geometry robust rather than tuned to slalom.
